reviews.summary: The lead, effort table, film tiers, running order and carving timing answer the search, but the table offers a dinner for two that the post never explains, and the film night says 4 hours while its running order runs 4½.

Every product, date, film and source claim checked out. Asked for 'many places' instead of 'most places' for the porch-light custom, US/UK-neutral 'sweater' and 'plastic bag' instead of 'jumper' and 'bin bag', and 'poniendo buena cara' for a Spanish line that read translated.

Beats page one's unsorted listicles with the effort table, running order and dated carving advice, but every top result covers themed food at home and the post only names a dinner in the table; the occasion-page link promised 'more ideas for the night' when that page is about the gift.

applied: New section 'A Halloween dinner for two' after the costumes, both languages.
Film night is 4½ hours in the table (4 horas y media).
Porch light: 'in many places, especially in North America' (ES matches).
'orange sweater', 'an opened-out plastic bag' (ES 'una bolsa de plástico abierta'); ES 'poniendo buena cara'.
Occasion-page link now says it covers what to write, what to add and when to send it.

Polish taken: 'aún le queda valor'; Scream swapped for The Sixth Sense / El sexto sentido in the in-between tier; 'book now' instead of 'this week' on a Friday; gift paragraph trimmed so it doesn't repeat the occasion page; older post's Spanish says 'el horario de la noche'.
rejected: Polish not taken: a note on The Shining's running time, and a treat-hunt item (both add text without fixing anything).

reviews.summary: Instead of a 40-item list it sorts a handful of ideas by effort, with a timed film-night running order, scare-graded films, a dated carving plan backed by Cornell, ten-minute costumes and lines you'd actually send.
Round-one fixes all made correctly and every claim verified. New text needed 'ready-made' instead of British 'shop-bought', and 'más que suficientes' to agree with 'unos brownies'.

Page one gives 20 to 40 one-line ideas with no way to choose; this sorts them by effort, adds a timed film night with graded films, carve-by dates for Saturday 31 October 2026 with a Cornell source, ten-minute costumes and lines to send.

applied: Polish taken to head off the same US/UK fix: 'turn the overhead light off'.

reviews.summary: The top results list forty interchangeable ideas; this sorts them by effort and gives a dated carve plan, a film running order with scare levels and costumes you can make tonight, so a couple can pick one and do it this week.
Round-two fixes made correctly; every product, date, film, Spain title and source claim checks out against the code and the cited pages, and the Spanish reads as written in Spain.

Page one is unranked lists of 10 to 40 ideas with no dates or way to choose; this sorts by effort, sets everything to the 2026 calendar and gives a film running order and lines to send, so it's the one page you can act on tonight.

rejected: Final-round polish recorded, not applied (RUBRIC step 4): a red skirt for Velma, 'candy' for US readers, an escape room, a treat hunt, baking together, and 'Empezad' for 'Empieza' in the Spanish opening.
